page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz, with a single thread per core and dedicated CPU allocation. The memory configuration consists of 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. Cache resources include 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 36 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, and operates on the Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 67 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier memory performance, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 391.76 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 185.65 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance is strong, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 21681.0 and robust software compilation capabilities, scoring 49127.0 in Clang compilation. Database operations are highly efficient, scoring in the top 10% on Passmark database tests and achieving 67.07 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. However, single-core CPU performance and LLM inference tasks, particularly text generation on small models and prompt processing on large models, fall into the average to weak categories.

The c8gb.8xlarge offers a resource-dense profile for compute-heavy workloads that benefit from high memory bandwidth and dedicated ARM64 cores without the overhead of hyperthreading. Given its lack of local storage, it relies on network-attached storage, making it suitable for containerized microservices, high-throughput web serving, software compilation pipelines, and database workloads that leverage its memory throughput.
